sentences.text: Now I was far enough south that I didn't get impacted by the fire.
This meeting is being recorded.
It was pretty gnarly there for a bit.
Yeah.
God.
Nightmare, huh?
Unbelievable.
I mean, whole area is just completely disappeared.
It's hard to believe.
I mean, we lived in LA for six months in 23.
So yeah, I've been to the Palisades a lot and lots of memories there, but it's just, it's unbelievable to see it now.
Just complete devastation.
Looks like a war zone.
Whereabouts are you based?
I'm in El Segundo, so south of lax.
Oh yeah, we were in Manhattan beach, so not, not too far.
Nice.
It's cool.
Nice.
It's nice.
Where are you?
Whereabouts are you now?
Well, back in the UK at the moment and I don't know how well you know, but we're in Somerset, which is in the southwest, about an hour and a half out of London.
Cool.
Nice.
Yeah, but we are actually, we're based in.
In London.
London.
Where are we at the moment?
London, New York and San Francisco where we are at the moment.
Cool.
Okay.
Right, so these calls are obviously bit of a.
A get to know session.
I don't know how much you know about capital A, but we're an M and A advisory for marketing services companies.
So we work both on the buy and the sell side.

Our sell side is agencies, co and our buy side, we work with growing marketing agencies, sort of midsize agencies, and also private equity, private investors as well, helping them to acquire companies.
So, yeah, it'd be good to find out a little bit about you and what it is that you're doing.
Yeah, first and Third and how we can help you.
Yeah, So I started first and third 12 years ago.

I have a development background and kind of was doing the freelance thing for a while and more and more clients wanted work, so kind of built up the agency and now we are a team of 15, I think full time.
And then we have a team of about seven contractors that we bring in as needed.
We do design and development mostly in the Shopify and WordPress space.
So we kind of have two what we call pods for our agency is one is on commerce and one is on content.
So that the commerce side is Shopify, the content side is WordPress.
Everything from redesigns, migrations, ongoing retainers, pretty much not industry specific as of right now, but we're starting to figure out how to drum up some business.
We've been pretty much referral and word of mouth for 12 years and I want to start to be able to control some of the deal flow.
So we're.
We hired a salesperson end of last year.

We hired a marketing contractor beginning of the year starting to create some content, starting to create some landing pages, buy some ads, trying to automate some of that pipeline versus just wait for the referrals to come in.
Last year we did, I think we were about 2.4 and we've been.
I feel like we're hitting a little bit of a ceiling there in terms of just getting consistent deals in on the referral side of things.
So that's where I want to figure out ways to, to get people that don't know us to find us.
And so I think when, when you guys reached out, I don't know, I'm still figuring out what the long term vision is, if we want to sell or if we want to merge or if we want to acquire.
It's early days on all of that stuff.
But I think for me we have an amazing team that can design and develop pretty much anything all day long.
That is our bread and butter.
Our struggle is finding those clients that need us.

And so when you reached out and there was like a roll up idea, if there was an agency that maybe didn't have the expertise, chops as much but had an audience that seems like something that could, or maybe it's a branding and agency that, that does really good branding work but maybe doesn't do web or design or development or something along those lines.
I think that that is something that we've done strategic partnerships with in the past.
And so yeah, I think that that's kind of the gist of it.
What would you say your, your EBITDAR is?
Do you know what that is?
Your profit margin on the 2.4?
Yeah.
So I think last year.
Let me pull it up.
Our profit margin, we want to be in the 15 range, but I think last year we were at 5 so 6, 5.7.
So not quite where we want to be.
I take a pretty, I take a salary because I got kids and I need to like make sure that I have consistent income in so that that number is inflated a little bit.
But I think we want to be in the 15% profit margin range and we're a little lower than that right now.
Okay.
What would you say is holding you back from doing the biz dev yourself?
Is there a reason why you can't do it or you've not been able to hire that type of person into the team?
I think it's just, it's not I get pulled into the business a lot, me and my coo.
When things get crazy, we get pulled in and that pulls us away from the kind of like outreach.
And it feels like whenever we need a client, a new client, somebody comes knocking on our doorstep, which is nice.
So luckily we haven't gotten to the point where we needed to be really proactive on the outreach side.
We do do things like every day we send an email out to somebody that we haven't talked to in a while just to like reconnect.
So we are very top of mind and we do have strategic partnerships with Shopify and WordPress and WP Engine that bring us leads when they have them.
But.
But again, it's not on our terms.
Right.
We don't get.
We're not able to say, wow, we need a client in April.
Let's turn something up to get that.
Like, we don't have those levers.
And that's the next step.
We started an ad campaign last week for our first time.
We're building landing pages, we're building content.
We did a webinar.
So we're doing, starting to do the right things.
But it's early days, right?
Okay, sounds like you're doing more than enough.
I mean, the business is doing well.
It's not that it's a bad business.
It looks, looks pretty good.
What's the idea behind, you know, maybe the idea of a rollup over just going to market and selling the business?
I mean, is there a kind of a number that you're trying to get to before you feel that, that it's worth your while?
I don't know.
I think I gotta probably reflect a little bit on that, on what I want to do long term.
I think part of me likes the idea of selling it and trying something new.
The other part of me wants to, like this might sound cliche, but build an empire, right, Where a bunch of different businesses got a lot of ideas, we have a lot of little side projects.
I think one thing that I've been playing around with is, is first and third is a business that builds businesses.
And this agency is just the, the engine that helps facilitate that.
So we have that awesome team that can pretty much tackle anything.
So the first business we're playing around with this idea of niching down into the fashion space on, on one of like a sub brand.
So we go target all fashion, Shopify plus brands and really create a sub brand around that and create content around that.
And so that that part of the business gets me really excited and like I feel like there's a lot of potential there also in the AI space starting to play there.
I think that gets me excited but at the same time AI is also terrifying because it's going to be race to the bottom on developers, race to the bottom on design.
And I feel like that's one of our strengths in addition to strategy.
But AI might just eat agencies lunch all day long.
So that makes me.
It won't eat yours, but it's going to eat your team's.
Yeah, yeah, so, so I think that's why there's, I don't think I have a clear.
I wish I was like this is what I want to do.
Like I, I don't have that long term thought yet and so that's why I just want to talk and see what you've been seeing out there.
What, what you and kind of get your take on like look, I would love to be a 10 million dollar agency and I don't have to and I just get to do the fun stuff where I get to solve problems.
That's the dream.
Well, I think, I think you can be Greg.
So I think you've got all the fundamental pieces.
Firstly there's you.
You seem extremely credible, you seem like a good guy and you seem young enough to have another 10 years in you to build, build an empire that there's no doubt there.
Plus first and Third is a great brand.
You can see that it looks really, really strong.
You're doing good work with good clients and the partnerships obviously at the level Of Shopify and WordPress as well, you know, that's as good as it gets in your space.
And I think the other piece possibly is like positioning and geography as well.
You know, you're in la, which is a great, a top tier city globally and people want to work with LA agencies.
I mean that's the top draw really.
I think even above New York and London is certainly the LA sort of credibility and design work that's done out there is the best in the world.
So okay, so I think your position.
We'Ve been remote for, since day one so I don't think about that.
Like it's really interesting you say that.
I got a noodle on that a little bit because I think there is something there and I just sometimes forget that it.
I'm in LA and that is a big market.

Not, not so long ago we went to market with a, a very small direct consumer agency that was based in la is actually an Aussie Australian fella that had moved out to Los Angeles a few years ago to, to open up a branch of an Australian agency and they kind of orphaned him and left him there to run it on his own.
But, but he, he had a great personality.
He's a really good guy.
But we went to market with that DTC agency.
We had 45 signed NDAs within 24 hours just because it was in LA.
I mean DTC is also a very good space to be in, but because it was in LA as well, everybody just wanted a piece of it because it's a footprint that everybody wants because the reputation is the best.
So I think just the fact and first and Third is a good name.
I mean you've got some good stuff going on.
It's a great business, I think.
And also one thing that I've seen, I've seen this done a few times across the US and in the UK and it works really well.
Where there's this kind of VC model, there's actually a really great one in, in Los Angeles that I've been talking to as well.

And what you do is you offer all of the marketing services, the ability to, to help develop brands, put them in, in front of more audience and you take a piece of it, you know, so there's this company is taking 5 or 10% of businesses and helping build them.
I can tell you you've already thought about this is a model and for somebody like yourself, like I say, very credible and a likable person with a great strong reputation already.
I mean your, your company is big.
2 1/2 million as well.
There's not many businesses that are that big.
It, I think when you're in la, it feels like two and a half mils.
Nothing.
Yeah, because that'll buy you like a parking space somewhere.
Yeah, yeah, for sure.
Yeah.
But actually no businesses get, get to that size.
You know, statistically it's, it's very small.
So you're already a very credible person to go out and, and help other smaller businesses to get to where you are.

The nice thing about doing that is that, you know, there's what we call multiple arbitrage, which is basically because your business is a certain size, it will, it will get a certain multiple when you go to market.
If you want to sell your business, you'll probably get a four or five times multiple and EBITDA.
So you're probably worth about 1.5, 1.25, 1.5 somewhere around there already.

But if you get these other, other businesses into your group, even if they're fairly small, they all become worth five times the EBITDA as well, which means that you can grow in value very quickly by just adding quite small businesses to what you're doing.
And there's your empire instantaneously added to what you're doing.
So all of it is there for you.
The other route would be that you go to market and sell the business.
I mean, it's worth 1.25.
1.5, which obviously will buy you a car and a.
Yeah, yeah, right.
I can buy half a house.
Yeah.
So.
So of no use what whatsoever.
Unless you move.
Move out to Austin with everybody else.
But.
But then you'll get nothing for your house because it will get taken in tax.
But.
But that is the other option.
So I think definitely you're on the right track with what you're thinking.
I think you just need to put it together and, and do it.
How can we help?
Well, we can certainly help you with that.
And again, you probably want to test the market yourself before you come to somebody like us, but we are able to.
To scale up those types of efforts.
So, for instance, we.
We work on the buy side.
We had a couple of guys start working with us.
One was in Miami, the other guy was.
Can't remember where he was.
Somewhere really boring.
In north.
In the north somewhere.
But basically they bought and sold companies for a long time and just retired and gone to the golf course.
But they realized they had one.
One more in them, only 52, 53 years old.
And they came to us and they were just like, stuck.
They tried to buy companies, but it was a lot of work.
But we've done two transactions with them.
They're about to do two little ones, and we're about to do two more.
And we're about nine months into the relationship, so something that would have taken them about three years, four years to do.
We've been able to compress that right down to about seven, eight months for them to do it.
So when you're at that point where you're ready and you need to work with somebody like us, we can really help you scale up those acquisitions.
But I think the first couple you'll probably be able to do on your own.
What does a little acquisition look like?
Well, you're blessed in the US because you have something called SBA lenders, so you have up to 5 million on tap, which is partially guaranteed by the government.
I mean, you still have to put a guarantee to it.
It's not perfect, but it does mean that you have this kind of tap for a sort of Three to five times multiple acquisition.
So you could buy a very successful business that was say doing million dollars in revenue, maybe 25% margin, something like that.
And you could buy that for, for 1 million.
They would supply the cash for you.
You'd be able to cash flow out of its own cash flow and obviously grow it within your own business.
So you would probably be able to pay it off much quicker than, than you would need to.
But also the other thing about the value of your company, because you're a 5x or a 6x, it's already worth half a million more as soon as you, you, you sign the contract and.
Interesting.
So are you typically the ones to go out like if, if.
Let's say we were at the point where it's like hey, we really want to.

Well, I want to go to two different ways like so I'm very intrigued by the, the VC model, but that sounds like it'd be early stage like ideas or is the VC model still work with existing businesses that you're just kind of almost like a whole.
So it is existing businesses, products already created.
You know, they've already done that first round where they, they've had a bit of growth but they've hit a ceiling really quickly and they don't know how to do the next bit.
So there's a lot of people that have great ideas for products.
You know, they build their first world.
They go to Shopify and they just set their own Shopify up and they get to a quick limit of, of, you know, sort of digital marketing expertise.
They run out quite quickly, but they have great products and great businesses.
You know, they'll be doing hundreds of thousands in revenue, but they just can't get beyond that.
And that's where you come in.
Professionalize the store, help them with their marketing, help them their mailing list, etc.
Etc.
And you can grow the business very quickly and take percentage of the company as well.
So yeah, I mean it's, it's a great, it's a great model and I've seen some really good companies do it.
There's one called Neon Flux actually which you should check out because they do.
They're in the beauty space really, but it's quite similar space to the fashion thing.
So yeah.
So are you guys.
So where do you fit in in this?
Are you finding the potential businesses?
If I said, hey, I, I want this type of business, I'm looking for these types of businesses and you go out and find them or are you facilitating.
Yeah, exactly.
That the whole the whole shebang.
The whole shebang.
We do, we do everything.
So basically you would say, look, I want, I want companies this size in this geography, etc.
Etc.
You tell us, you know, what services they do, what verticals they're in, we go out and find them, we talk to them and we bring them into the conversation and get the deal across the line.
Because we're an M and A advisory, we can do the whole journey.
But we've actually just acquired a company ourselves called Deal Engines.
And Deal Engines will just do the actual deal flow for you.
So it's not as sort of intimate, we don't get as involved.
But we find all the deals for you.
We just stick them in your calendar rather than do the work for you.
So, so it depends on the scale that you want.
Some, some people are more hands on, others understand it, it does take a lot of work.
You know, once you've spoken to you know, 15, 20 agencies, it gets very boring very fast and it blurs.
You know, you can't remember who is who.

But we do all of that work and you end up then just having like a final race with three or four that you really, really love and you haven't had to speak to like 20 before that so you're not exhausted and you can get deals closed much, much more easily.
So we do do that.
But also the idea of the, the rollup is, and it's funny because I, I do speak to a lot of Shopify agencies that, that actually push that rollup thing in my, my mailing list.

But what we do in the rollups is we, we basically just sit on a bunch of contacts that say that they're interested in being rolled up and when we've got four or five together then we, we go, we put them together in a, in a sort of virtual room and then we, we go to a bigger agency that's looking for a Shopify agency that's this big.
You know, a lot of bigger agencies, they can't buy, you know, businesses that are doing two and a half million, they need to buy like a 10 million plus business.
So we, we put them all together in a package and put them in front of these larger agencies and it makes it easier for everybody to get the transaction done.
And like I said, with the multiple arbitrage, instead of Everybody being worth a 4x, they would be worth 5, 6, 7x depending on how big we can get the group to.
So, so that's the type of thing we do in the roll up space.
So it really does depend.
Everybody's at a different stage.
And I would say, you know, I'm an entrepreneur as well.
My background is, is in marketing.
I sold my business 2016.
I would say the first route that you do, you need to exhaust really is to go and build the empire.
If you haven't exhausted yourself doing that yet, then that's definitely the first way to go.
Because otherwise you end up just working for somebody else for three years.
I mean, it's still good.
You still get a couple of mil in the bank, but it's not.
That sounds nice, but yes, it's not.
Yeah.
The return is not as high as.
The potential return is not as high if you're just.
Yeah, exactly.
I got some left in the tank.
Yeah.
Now you look like you go.
I can see the whites of your eyes still.
You still look good.
Well, okay, so on the empire side of things, what does that even look like to start?
Like, what would you recommend me, even start to think about?
Cause look, I'm just building this, right?
We've got an agency, we work on good.
We work with good people and we do good things.
But I don't know, I've never been part of an acquisition before.
I've never even thought about why would somebody want to sell their agency or their brand or whatever like that even thought doesn't cross my mind very often.
Yeah, yeah.
So there's lots of different reasons.
They might just be tired, they might have taken as far as they can.
They might just be a creative and they didn't really intend to, to, to build a business.
And these are businesses of all different sizes.
It might just be a team of five or ten.
You know, it's.
It doesn't have to be something that's really established and, you know, sort of, you know, set out in a sort of a official way.
It can just be a group of freelancers with one guys who's winning the, the business.
You know, there's all, all sorts of different shapes out there.
How would, how would you go about it?
So the thing I always say is if you can run a business, you can make an acquisition.
They're no more complicated.
The fact that you've had to send all the forms off to the government to get yourself registered already is exactly the same thing.
There's no more complicated processes to do.
It is smoke and mirrors by accountants and lawyers who make it seem like it's more complicated than that.
It really isn't.
And so you, you're.
I mean, you can't do it by accident.
That's, that's one thing.
I mean, it does happen, but you have to put a certain amount of thought and effort into doing it, and the majority of that is actually just having those meetings.
So if you were to have.
I mean, if I.

If you said to me, now find me 20 Shopify agencies in LA or within 20 miles, if you spoke to 20 agencies, you would find two or three of those that will be ready to sell tomorrow for not very much money.
They just, they want to get out, they're stressed, they don't want to do the bills, they don't want to be responsible for people's salaries.
They want to sit in part of a bigger organization and just get back to designing or doing whatever they're passionate about.
It is just really that.

So once you start having those conversations, you'll realize that there are acquisitions to have and then the actual financial part of it is secondary almost, because some deals you could potentially close without very much money at all.
Interesting.
So is that, like, how does that.
So I'm guessing the 5 million on tap, what is that like a 30 or 10%, like interest loan?
Or how does that even work on the SBA side of things?
Can you really do an acquisition without really anything, any cash out of my bank?
So everybody wants skin in the game.
So there is always some blood money that you're gonna have to put in there.
Yeah.
So the SBA lenders, they tend to want you to put something in 20, 30%.
So it probably would restrict how big you could go on that first time round.
But once you've done one, it becomes a hell of a lot easier to finance the next deal.

And quite often you can go to special sort of acquisition lenders, M and A lenders, and they are more likely to see that you've got a track record doing something and put the money up in terms of interest rates and everything else.
They're just normal banks.
I mean, if you look at them, a lot of the SBA lenders are tiny little local banks that you've never heard of.
So they're just, they're lending on competitive rates to try and get the, the most business done.
I could put you in touch with somebody, it can give you some advice, but everybody's hands are tied until you've got a deal on the table.
And that's why I'm encouraging you to go out and speak to people first.
Once you've got a deal, you can take it to a lender and then they will tell you exactly how much they will lend.
And what the terms will be, but nobody can really say until that moment.
It's kind of catch 22 in that sense.
Got it.
Yeah, I get that.
Okay, so you, you made it.
And if you have to, if you have a hard stop, we can, we can call it.
But you had mentioned doing the first couple yourself.
What is, what is, what did you mean by that?
What, like.
Will have a network?
I think you might have been touched on it before.
Of companies, agencies, freelancers that they already deal with.
And those are the easy conversations to have.
I mean, I can't find, I can't have those conversations where I can't find those that are in your Rolodex already.
So I would say to anyone, just have those conversations first.
I mean, if I said to you, just think of those two little agencies that you always work with.
The one know, if you're over capacity, you'll go to them.
It's those guys.
They're the guys that you can say, look, we're interested in doing a couple acquisitions this year.
What is your thoughts on it?
If we were to make you an offer or if, if there is a way that we could merge our businesses and grow together and they'll have an opinion.
It's worth discussing.
There's probably 10, 10 of those that you could have in the next couple of weeks.
Yeah, okay.
That's lot of, lot of, put a lot of thinking in my, my brain that I need to do so.
I appreciate that.
Yeah, well, it's all there, Greg.
You know, we speak to a lot of people.
Some people aren't, aren't the type.
You know, I always say, you know, we speak to a lot of people.
They don't have the kahunas to, to do the deal.

So I can talk to people all day, but I, I, I sense that there is, there's something in you, you know, if you're looking to build that empire that, that you, you're the guy, you need to put that empire together.
It could be huge in the next five to 10 years.
If you've got a strategy to, to acquire smaller businesses, you can go and go and go, and you can be worth a hell of a lot of money at the end of it.
So.
Well, that sounds, that sounds appealing to me.
Yeah.
Well, let's do it.

I'm happy, I'm happy to help you out, but like I said, I think the majority of it you can do in the first instance yourself, but certainly when you get to the size where you need me, or if you feel confident enough to Invest in my team, then, then we're here.
But it's $5,000 a month.
We take one and a half percent on the deal.
If you get an SBA lender, they will cover a banker's fees.
That's pretty standard.
So if you just went, you know, this is the price we're paying, this is the 1/2% for the banker's fees.
It all stacks up and they're happy with that.
But we, we can put those deals together as, like I say, have those little conversations first.
And if you feel really confident, think, do you know what, Andy?
I want to do this strategy with you and I want to work with your team.
We can bring those deals to the table.
We can get deals done very, very quickly.
Once you're, once you're rolling SBA advisors that will be able to find you the loans as well.
Is there a, obviously we're not in the space right now where, like it would even make sense.
And, and I think this is why you're saying go out and have those conversations yourself.
Is there a smaller engagement where it's like more of a consulting in the early stages?
Just like, Because I don't, I don't know what I'm doing.
I can have conversations, but I don't know what a good deal looks like versus not.
And I kind of need to like, obviously have a lot of conversations to figure out numbers and see if what makes sense.
But I think.
Is there a, like a consult consultancy type of thing with you?
And yeah, we do actually.
So I've got Agencies X, which is what I call an accelerator.
So Agencies X dot com.
It's just a, it's a form.
If you, if you are interested, just put in your details.
It's an accelerator and it's, it's not quite one to one.
It's kind of a, it's a cross between like a group thing.
We do have one to one sessions as well.
There's lots of videos and sort of stuff that I can, I give, you know, like spreadsheets that help you calculate valuations and things like that.
Um, so yeah, we can do, we can do something like, I can send you more details.
Yeah.
And that, that takes you through exactly the process that we do for our clients.
So it just shows you exactly what we're doing.
And it's super cheap as well right now because I want to, I want to get like 20 testimonials.
So I'm doing it for like a tenth of the price.
But yeah, I can send you some, some details on Agencies X.
And that shows you exactly how to do it.
My personal take on this is that there's no magic involved in M and A.
I think people talk about it as if it's this really weird thing, but it really isn't.
It just is start.
They're starting your own business and then there's buying somebody else's business.
It's just exactly the same thing.
Only one you put loads of energy into for 10 years and the other you don't have to.
That's a good way to phrase it.
Makes it very appealing.
Um, well, thanks, Andy.
Like, I appreciate it.
Yeah, send me that information.
I think I'm curious.
So, yeah, I think that sounds like a good, good first step is to check that out.
Yeah, brilliant.
Okay, I'll be happy to.
And I'll be happy to work with someone like you, Greg.
Like I said, I think you've got all the pieces already there that you need to get there.
So it's not.
It's not too much work, I don't think, to make that first acquisition.
And once you make the first one, I've actually got some podcasts up.
If you look up M and a Q and A podcast there, there's probably about 15, I think.
And every.
Every guest on there is somebody that's made an acquisition.
But I.
I interviewed this one guy.
He's part of a.
Well, he's the founder of a 200 million agency that was bought by Samsung.
And he said he just wishes that he'd started doing acquisitions earlier, because as soon as he did that first one, he realized how he could do it again and again and again.
And they've.
They've gone on to grow.
I mean, they've been acquired, I think two or three times themselves, called Iris Worldwide.
But, yeah, they've acquired like 20 agencies easily, maybe.
Maybe more than that.
And now they're funded by the bank of Korea.
They could just buy whatever they want.
So.
That's amazing.
Wow.
Incredible.
Yeah.
Cool.
I will check that out again.
Thank you for.
For all your wisdom.
And let's stay in touch.
Yeah, my pleasure.
I will.
I'll ping you an email in the next couple of days, give you some more information on Agencies X, and we can get started with that if you want.
It's just a nice easy way to get your toe in the water.
And I show you exactly what we're doing and you can just go out and do it yourself, or we can help you either way.
All right, Have a good day.
Enjoy the rest of the day.
I'll speak to you soon.
